post.caption: This pink pearl comes from a snail. It comes from the queen conch, a large Caribbean sea snail, and unlike an oyster pearl, a conch pearl has no nacre. Its surface has a shimmering pattern called flame structure, and parallel fibers of aragonite crystal create that silky shimmer. Collectors prize pink stones, especially a salmon pink. Reportedly, about one conch in 10,000 makes a pearl. Conch pearls were popular in Victorian jewelry, then revived in the 1980s. In 2024, the United States listed the queen conch as threatened. In 2009, researchers developed a technique to seed conch pearls.
